ev.mng_d_dzud.title: Dzud
ev.mng_d_dzud.text: After a rainy autumn came a hard frost, and the whole steppe is sealed under a crust of ice. The sheep cannot break it with their hooves, and the horses gnaw one another's manes. They say that beyond the pass, three days' ride away, the snow is loose and there is grass beneath it.
ev.mng_d_dzud.far_pasture: Drive the herd over the pass
ev.mng_d_dzud.far_pasture.success: You bring the herd through to the loose snow. In spring you have more lambs than any of your neighbours, and people tell the story of your crossing round their hearths.
ev.mng_d_dzud.far_pasture.failure: A blizzard caught you on the pass. Half the herd lay down in the snow, and you barely made it back with frostbitten hands.
ev.mng_d_dzud.slaughter: Slaughter the weak before they die
ev.mng_d_dzud.slaughter.ok: You slaughter the weak ones for meat and hides. The strong ones last until spring, and the frozen meat sells in town.
ev.mng_d_dzud.ask_noyan.ok: The noyan gives hay from his stores but writes down the debt. The herd is almost whole - and the debt grows.
ev.mng_d_dzud_debt.title: The hay debt
ev.mng_d_dzud_debt.text: The noyan's man has come for the debt for that hay in the dzud. You have nothing to pay with - so he offers: give your best horse against the debt, or work a year as a herdsman with his horses.
ev.mng_d_dzud_debt.horse.ok: You give up the horse. The debt is cleared, but spring is hard without it.
ev.mng_d_dzud_debt.work.ok: For a year you herd another man's horses. But you learn a great deal from the old horse-herders.
ev.mng_d_anda.title: Anda
ev.mng_d_anda.text: Your best playmate offers to become anda - sworn brothers. As Temüjin and Jamukha once did, you will exchange gifts: an anklebone, a whistling arrow. An anda is closer than a brother: he shares your last cup, and your death.
ev.mng_d_anda.swear.ok: You drink from one cup and mix your blood. Now you have an anda.
ev.mng_d_anda.wait.ok: Your friend is hurt but says nothing. Perhaps it really is too soon.
ev.mng_d_anda_later.title: Your anda in trouble
ev.mng_d_anda_later.text: A rider brings word: enemies have fallen on your anda's camp, his herd is being driven off and he is wounded. To go means risking everything. Not to go means breaking the oath.
ev.mng_d_anda_later.ride.success: You win the herd back. Your anda embraces you before everyone: "Your life is my life."
ev.mng_d_anda_later.ride.failure: The enemy was too strong. You come back badly wounded, but your anda knows you came.
ev.mng_d_anda_later.stay.ok: You stay. Your anda survives, but he never rides to your yurt again.
ev.mng_d_bride.title: A bride from another clan
ev.mng_d_bride.text: A wife must come from another clan. You have long had your eye on a girl from the camp across the river, but her father asks a great bride-price - nine times nine head of livestock. Your friends laugh: "You could steal her, the old way. If they catch you, you pay them off."
ev.mng_d_bride.steal.success: She was waiting for you herself by the tethering post. Her kin grumble and agree to peace for a couple of horses.
ev.mng_d_bride.steal.failure: Her brothers caught you at the ford. You were beaten, and then you still had to pay for the insult.
ev.mng_d_bride.kalym.ok: Half the herd goes across the river, and a bride comes to you with her own yurt. The wedding lasts three days.
ev.mng_d_bride.wait.ok: You decide to wait until the herd has grown. Meanwhile another man comes courting her.
ev.mng_d_yasa_water.title: Heat and the yasa
ev.mng_d_yasa_water.text: Summer heat, everyone is covered in dust, and the river is right there. But the yasa forbids washing yourself or your clothes in running water in summer: the Sky, they say, grows angry and strikes with thunder. There is no one around... it seems.
ev.mng_d_yasa_water.bathe.success: The water is ice-cold and sweet. No one saw - only a sandpiper on the shallows.
ev.mng_d_yasa_water.bathe.failure: A herdsman from a neighbouring clan saw you. You had to pay a fine and endure sidelong looks for a week.
ev.mng_d_yasa_water.endure.ok: You wipe yourself down with a damp cloth by the yurt, like everyone else. The yasa is the yasa.
ev.mng_d_stray_horse.title: Someone else's horse
ev.mng_d_stray_horse.text: A stranger's horse has joined your herd - a good one, with an unfamiliar tamga on its rump. By the yasa, whoever keeps another's horse pays nine like it, and if he cannot, gives up his children. But the owner may be a hundred versts away.
ev.mng_d_stray_horse.return.ok: A month later the owner comes for the horse and leaves you a sheep in thanks.
ev.mng_d_stray_horse.keep.success: No one came looking. The horse grazes in your herd.
ev.mng_d_stray_horse.keep.failure: The owner knew his horse by its colour and a scar. Judgement was swift: a fine of nine head.
ev.mng_d_pasture.title: A quarrel over pasture
ev.mng_d_pasture.text: A neighbouring camp has pitched its yurts on your autumn pasture - the meadow where your family has grazed its herds since your grandfathers' day. Their young men are already sharpening knives and saying the steppe belongs to no one.
ev.mng_d_pasture.fight.success: You drive the strangers out, and their headman sends a horse as a token of peace.
ev.mng_d_pasture.fight.failure: The fight turns bloody. The meadow stays theirs, and you are left with a wound and missing sheep.
ev.mng_d_pasture.yield.ok: You lead the herd to a far meadow. The grass is poorer, but there is no blood.
ev.mng_d_pasture.noyan.ok: The noyan hears both sides, takes gifts from both and judges by the old boundaries. The meadow is yours.
ev.mng_d_horse_thieves.title: Horse thieves
ev.mng_d_horse_thieves.text: In the night the dogs set up a clamour, and in the morning half the horse herd is gone. In the snow there are tracks - strange horses heading south. You can still catch them if you ride now.
ev.mng_d_horse_thieves.chase.success: You catch the thieves at a well and win the herd back. Two of them are tied up and taken for judgement.
ev.mng_d_horse_thieves.chase.failure: There were more of them. You come back with an arrow in your shoulder and no horses.
ev.mng_d_horse_thieves.track.ok: A month later some of the horses turn up at a far market. The rest are lost.
ev.mng_d_wrestling.title: Wrestlers at the festival
ev.mng_d_wrestling.text: At the summer festival come the "three manly games": racing, archery and wrestling. Wrestlers in short jackets dance the "eagle's flight" before each bout. The loser is the first to touch the ground with anything but his feet.
ev.mng_d_wrestling.enter.success: You throw five men and win the title of "falcon". They present you with a horse and a bowl of kumis.
ev.mng_d_wrestling.enter.failure: In the second round you are thrown over a hip. Your shoulder aches for a month.
ev.mng_d_wrestling.watch.ok: You shout yourself hoarse for your camp's wrestler. He reaches the seventh round.
ev.mng_d_wrestling_later.title: A wrestler for the noyan
ev.mng_d_wrestling_later.text: The noyan remembers you from the festival and summons you to wrestle for his camp at the khan's great gathering. A win would be glory for the whole clan.
ev.mng_d_wrestling_later.go.success: You reach the final round. The noyan takes you among his nökers.
ev.mng_d_wrestling_later.go.failure: You are thrown in the third round. The noyan shrugs and forgets you.
ev.mng_d_wrestling_later.no.ok: You plead a sore shoulder. The noyan is displeased.
ev.mng_d_archery.title: The archery contest
ev.mng_d_archery.text: The targets are little leather cylinders stacked into a wall five hundred paces off. Each archer looses four arrows, and the judges sing a long "uukhai" after every hit. Women and girls are not forbidden to shoot.
ev.mng_d_archery.shoot.success: Three arrows of four hit the wall. The judges sing "uukhai" for you three times.
ev.mng_d_archery.shoot.failure: The wind carries your arrows wide. People tease you about it till evening.
ev.mng_d_archery.skip.ok: You watch from the side, chewing aaruul.
ev.mng_d_nerge.title: The great hunt
ev.mng_d_nerge.text: In winter the khan holds a nerge, the great ring hunt. For a month thousands of riders tighten a circle a hundred versts across, driving the game inwards. To let a beast out of the ring is a disgrace, and punished. A wounded boar is charging straight at you.
ev.mng_d_nerge.hold.success: The boar is on your spear. The commander of the hundred nods approvingly - this will reach the khan.
ev.mng_d_nerge.hold.failure: The boar bowls over your horse. You lie up with a torn leg, and the boar gets away.
ev.mng_d_nerge.let_pass.success: The boar shoots past you - into the next hundred. No one can tell whose fault it was.
ev.mng_d_nerge.let_pass.failure: The commander saw. You are flogged before the ranks and stripped of your share of the game.
ev.mng_d_sick_child.title: A child's fever
ev.mng_d_sick_child.text: {npc} has been burning with fever for three days and will take neither milk nor broth. Over the door of the yurt a cord with a red rag already hangs - the sign that someone inside is ill and strangers must keep out.
ev.mng_d_sick_child.shaman.success: The shaman drums till dawn and draws the sickness out into a black kid. The fever breaks.
ev.mng_d_sick_child.shaman.failure: The drum does not help. {npc} goes to the ancestors at dawn.
ev.mng_d_sick_child.physician: Fetch the physician from the court
ev.mng_d_sick_child.physician.success: The physician feels the pulse, sets needles and gives a bitter draught. Two days later {npc} asks for food.
ev.mng_d_sick_child.kumis.success: You never leave the bed; you feed kumis by the spoonful and wrap the child in sheepskin. The fever recedes.
ev.mng_d_sick_child.kumis.failure: The little body did not have the strength.
ev.mng_d_orphan.title: A foundling in a ruined camp
ev.mng_d_orphan.text: In a plundered Tatar camp they find a boy in a sable cap with gold earrings. Chinggis Khan's mother Hö'elün, they say, took in just such a child and raised him as her son - he became the chief judge of the empire. The child looks at you and says nothing.
ev.mng_d_orphan.adopt.ok: You lift the boy onto your horse. Now you have one more child.
ev.mng_d_orphan.refuse.ok: Another family takes the boy. Sometimes you see him at the festival.
ev.mng_d_feud.title: Blood for blood
ev.mng_d_feud.text: Men of a neighbouring clan have killed a kinsman of yours at the watering place. By steppe custom blood is paid with blood - or with livestock, if both sides agree. The old men are waiting for your word.
ev.mng_d_feud.revenge.success: You drive off their herd and burn their wagons. Your clan is satisfied - but the feud is not over.
ev.mng_d_feud.revenge.failure: They were waiting for you. You barely escape alive.
ev.mng_d_feud.price.ok: Their elders drive over nine horses and nine camels. Peace is made, though a bitter one.
ev.mng_d_feud.forgive: Forgive for the sake of peace
ev.mng_d_feud.forgive.ok: You say: "The Sky will judge." Many take it for weakness.
ev.mng_d_feud_later.title: The return raid
ev.mng_d_feud_later.text: The hostile clan comes back by night. Dogs bark, the felt of a neighbouring yurt is burning, arrows whistle in the dark.
ev.mng_d_feud_later.defend.success: The raid is beaten off. The old men say they will not try again for a long while.
ev.mng_d_feud_later.defend.failure: They drive off part of the herd and vanish into the night.
ev.mng_d_feud_later.flee: Lead the children out into the steppe
ev.mng_d_feud_later.flee.ok: You lead the children and old folk into a gully. Afterwards the yurts had to be pitched anew.
ev.mng_d_captive_master.title: Your share of the captives
ev.mng_d_captive_master.text: After a city is taken the captives are shared out by tens: craftsmen apart - they are spared. Your share is a grey-haired smith from Khwarazm with his tools. He says he can make blades such as the steppe has never seen.
ev.mng_d_captive_master.take.ok: The smith sets up his forge by your yurt. The neighbours are already bringing him bits and cauldrons.
ev.mng_d_captive_master.free.ok: The old man weeps and kisses your stirrup. Whether he will make it home, who knows.
ev.mng_d_captive_master.sell.ok: The merchant leads the smith off with his caravan to Karakorum. The silver weighs pleasantly on your belt.
ev.mng_d_captive_later.title: The smith's blade
ev.mng_d_captive_later.text: Your Khwarazmian smith has forged a sabre patterned like water in the wind. The noyan, seeing it, offers ten horses for it - and the smith quietly asks to be allowed to go to his son in Samarkand.
ev.mng_d_captive_later.sell: Sell the sabre to the noyan
ev.mng_d_captive_later.sell.ok: Ten horses join your herd. The smith lowers his eyes.
ev.mng_d_captive_later.free: Free the smith, sabre and all
ev.mng_d_captive_later.free.ok: You send him off with a caravan. A year later a parcel arrives from Samarkand: silk and a note in Uyghur letters.
ev.mng_d_slave_flight.title: An unguarded herd
ev.mng_d_slave_flight.text: Your masters are feasting in the great yurt, the horse-herder is asleep. The wind blows from the west - from where, a week's ride away, lies your homeland. The yasa orders a captured runaway returned to his master and anyone who hides him put to death.
ev.mng_d_slave_flight.run.success: For three nights you ride without a fire. On the fourth morning you are among strangers - but free.
ev.mng_d_slave_flight.run.failure: They catch you on the second day. You are beaten long and hard and returned to your master.
ev.mng_d_slave_flight.stay.ok: You lie down at the threshold and listen to the wind.
ev.mng_d_paiza_demand.title: A man with a paiza
ev.mng_d_paiza_demand.text: A rider has come up to the camp with a silver paiza at his neck - a tablet bearing the khan's word: "Whoever does not obey shall die." He demands five fresh horses, a sheep and lodging for his retinue. He is the third this spring.
ev.mng_d_paiza_demand.give.ok: You hand over the horses. Whether you will ever see them again is another matter.
ev.mng_d_paiza_demand.hide: Drive the herd into a gully
ev.mng_d_paiza_demand.hide.success: The courier rides off empty-handed, cursing. The herd is safe.
ev.mng_d_paiza_demand.hide.failure: His men find the herd and take twice as much - "for the deceit".
ev.mng_d_paiza_demand.complain.ok: The governor listens. They say Khan Ögedei himself railed against those who use a paiza for their own gain.
ev.mng_d_ortaq.title: Silver for a partnership
ev.mng_d_ortaq.text: A noyan is looking for an ortaq - a partner to carry his silver with a caravan to Khwarazm or China. Profit shared, losses yours. Under the khan's protection the caravans travel in safety - but a desert is a desert.
ev.mng_d_ortaq.accept.success: The caravan comes back with silk and pearls. The noyan is pleased, and you are richer.
ev.mng_d_ortaq.accept.failure: Camels die in the sands, the goods are spoiled. The noyan demands his money back.
ev.mng_d_ortaq.refuse.ok: You keep to what you have. It is calmer that way.
ev.mng_d_drinking.title: The cup goes round
ev.mng_d_drinking.text: At the feast the noyan sends a great silver bowl round the circle. To refuse is to insult your host, and here they drink until the guests fall over. Chinggis Khan, they say, taught that a man may be drunk no more than three times a month.
ev.mng_d_drinking.drink.success: You last to the end and sing a song the noyan has you sing again.
ev.mng_d_drinking.drink.failure: In the morning they find you by the tethering post. And ever since, the cup pulls at you harder.
ev.mng_d_drinking.pour: Flick a drop for the spirits and only sip
ev.mng_d_drinking.pour.ok: You flick a drop to the Sky with your ring finger and only sip. Someone snorts, but you stay sober.
ev.mng_d_gamble.title: Playing for livestock
ev.mng_d_gamble.text: In winter there is little to do, and the men play shagai no longer for bones but for livestock: a sheep for a well-aimed flick, a horse for a loss. Someone holds out a handful of bones to you.
ev.mng_d_gamble.play.success: Flick after flick - and by morning two strangers' sheep stand in your pen.
ev.mng_d_gamble.play.failure: You lose more than you meant to, and you keep itching to win it back.
ev.mng_d_gamble.no.ok: You watch others lose their horses and are glad of your caution.
ev.mng_d_daughter_match.title: The matchmakers
ev.mng_d_daughter_match.text: {npc} is of an age to marry, and two matches are offered at once: {g=npc_sex:a rich noyan offers his daughter without asking any bride-price, while in the neighbouring camp there is a girl the groom has long been sighing over - but her father asks a great deal|a rich noyan's son brings a bride-price of a hundred head, while in the neighbouring camp there is a lad the bride has long been sighing over}.
ev.mng_d_daughter_match.noyan.ok: A rich wedding, and honour for the clan. But all through the feast {npc} keeps looking towards the neighbouring camp.
ev.mng_d_daughter_match.heart.ok: No wealth is gained, but {npc} glows so that the whole yurt is bright.
ev.mng_d_lightning.title: The wrath of the Sky
ev.mng_d_lightning.text: Lightning has struck a neighbouring yurt and killed two horses. There is nothing the Mongols fear more than thunder. The shaman says the whole camp must be purified - passing between two fires, herds, goods and all.
ev.mng_d_lightning.fires.ok: Smoke, crackling, bleating sheep - and your heart is lighter. The shaman gets a sheep for the rite.
ev.mng_d_lightning.ignore.ok: The neighbours shun your yurt as if the fire from the sky were still smoking on it.
ev.mng_d_ongon.title: The ongons
ev.mng_d_ongon.text: On the lattice of the yurt, above the master's place, hang the ongons - felt figures of the guardian ancestors. They must be "fed": their lips smeared with fat, kumis sprinkled on them. You have not done it for a long while, and things are going wrong at home.
ev.mng_d_ongon.feed.ok: You smear the felt lips with mutton fat. It seems the ancestors smile.
ev.mng_d_ongon.neglect.ok: You wave it away. Grandmother shakes her head and secretly smears their lips herself.
ev.mng_d_shaman_call.title: The call of the spirits
ev.mng_d_shaman_call.text: For a month you have been tormented by strange dreams: you fly over the steppe, you are taken apart bone by bone and put together again. An old udagan, a shaman woman, says it plainly: "The ancestor spirits have chosen you. Refuse, and they will torment you to death."
ev.mng_d_shaman_call.accept.ok: The udagan gives you her old drum and teaches you the rites. Now people come to you for help.
ev.mng_d_shaman_call.refuse.success: Little by little the dreams fade. Perhaps the spirits chose another.
ev.mng_d_shaman_call.refuse.failure: You go down with a fever, and the old woman only sighs: "I warned you."
ev.mng_d_nestorian.title: The Kereit cross
ev.mng_d_nestorian.text: A Nestorian priest with a Syriac book goes round the camps. The Kereits and Naimans have long been baptised, and at court many of the khans' wives are Christian. He says Christ is the Sky too - only the Sky that spoke to men.
ev.mng_d_nestorian.baptize.ok: The priest sprinkles you with water and gives you a little copper cross. The Sky, it seems, is not offended.
ev.mng_d_nestorian.both: Listen, but keep the old ways
ev.mng_d_nestorian.both.ok: You buy a little cross from him - just in case - to hang beside the ongons.
ev.mng_d_nestorian.no.ok: The priest bows and goes on to the next yurt.
ev.mng_d_islam_horde.title: The khan's faith
ev.mng_d_islam_horde.text: The khan has embraced Islam, and mosques now stand by the camp. Nobles who want his favour are learning the prayers. The old noyans grumble: "Chinggis's yasa is dearer to us than the books of the Arabs" - and some of them are no longer alive.
ev.mng_d_islam_horde.convert.ok: You recite the shahada in the camp mosque. The mullah gives you a new name - though your kin still call you by the old one.
ev.mng_d_islam_horde.old_way.ok: You still pray to the Sky - but now it is better not to say so aloud.
ev.mng_d_lamas.title: The Yellow Faith
ev.mng_d_lamas.text: Altan Khan has met a Tibetan lama and given him the title of Dalai Lama, and the lama in turn has declared the khan a rebirth of Khubilai. Now ongons are burned on bonfires, blood sacrifices are forbidden, and the lamas hand out prayer flags instead.
ev.mng_d_lamas.convert.ok: You give your ongons to the lama and receive a rosary. Now the yurt smells of juniper smoke.
ev.mng_d_lamas.shaman.ok: You sew the ongons into an old felt and feed them in secret.
ev.mng_d_son_to_monastery.title: A child for the monastery
ev.mng_d_son_to_monastery.text: The lamas say that every family should give at least one child to the monastery, and that this earns merit for a hundred rebirths. {npc} is quick-witted - they are ready to take {g=npc_sex:him|her} and teach Tibetan letters.
ev.mng_d_son_to_monastery.give: Give the child to the monastery
ev.mng_d_son_to_monastery.give.ok: {npc} rides away with the lamas in a red robe, never once looking back. You feel both proud and empty.
ev.mng_d_son_to_monastery.keep.ok: You say: "I need {g=npc_sex:him|her} at home." The lamas do not insist.
ev.mng_d_faith_debate.title: The debate of faiths
ev.mng_d_faith_debate.text: Khan Möngke has staged a debate at court: a Franciscan friar, Nestorian priests, Muslim mullahs and Buddhist monks must prove whose faith is best. Between rounds everyone drinks, and by evening the Nestorians are singing so loudly that no one can out-argue them.
ev.mng_d_faith_debate.christian.ok: The words about God become man will not leave your head.
ev.mng_d_faith_debate.muslim.ok: The mullah speaks briefly and clearly: God is one. That sounds like the Eternal Sky.
ev.mng_d_faith_debate.buddhist.ok: The monk speaks of rebirth and of how all living things suffer. You think about it for a long time.
ev.mng_d_faith_debate.drink: Drink with everyone and choose nothing
ev.mng_d_faith_debate.drink.ok: Like the khan, you conclude: "The fingers of one hand are different - and so are the faiths."
ev.mng_d_faith_debate.note: In May 1254, at the wish of Khan Möngke, a debate between representatives of different faiths was held in Karakorum. The Franciscan William of Rubruck took part and left a description of it. Möngke told him that as God gave the hand different fingers, so He gave men different ways.
ev.mng_d_chinese_ways.title: The brush or the bow
ev.mng_d_chinese_ways.text: A school has opened in Khanbaliq for Mongol children, teaching Chinese writing and the books of Confucius. The old men grumble that a Mongol who trades his bow for a brush is no Mongol. The teacher says an empire is not ruled with arrows.
ev.mng_d_chinese_ways.classics.ok: You trace characters until your wrist aches. The world of books is vast.
ev.mng_d_chinese_ways.steppe.ok: You drive your horse round the riding ground by the palace and shoot at a gourd on a pole.
ev.mng_d_classics_later.title: The examinations
ev.mng_d_classics_later.text: For the first time in many years the court has proclaimed examinations for office. The questions are easier for Mongols, but the places are few. Your Chinese learning may come in useful.
ev.mng_d_classics_later.sit.success: Your name is on the list of those who passed. You receive a post in the chancery.
ev.mng_d_classics_later.sit.failure: Your essay on filial duty proves weak. Perhaps in three years.
ev.mng_d_classics_later.skip.ok: You decide office is not worth the sleepless nights.
ev.mng_d_ransom.title: The ransom
ev.mng_d_ransom.text: A Russian priest of the Sarai diocese has come to you: he is collecting money to ransom captives and asks you to sell him your Novgorodian bondsman. He has little money, but he promises to pray for you.
ev.mng_d_ransom.sell.ok: The Novgorodian leaves with the priest, crossing himself. The silver is modest, but honest.
ev.mng_d_ransom.free.ok: The priest bows to the ground. For a long time afterwards the bazaar gossips about your generosity.
ev.mng_d_ransom.refuse.ok: A worker is more useful than prayers. The priest goes on to the next yard.
ev.mng_d_vykhod.title: To collect the tribute
ev.mng_d_vykhod.text: A baskak is gathering a troop to ride into Rus for the tribute - the "exit", as the Russians call it. From every household silver and furs, and from those who have nothing, people. It is profitable work, but in Russian towns the assembly bell may ring at any moment.
ev.mng_d_vykhod.go.success: You return with a train of sables and silver. Your share is worth a herd of five hundred head.
ev.mng_d_vykhod.go.failure: In Rostov the bell rang and the townsfolk cut down half the troop. You barely escaped the town.
ev.mng_d_vykhod.stay.ok: You prefer your own herd to other men's silver.
ev.mng_d_serve_moscow.title: Into Moscow's service
ev.mng_d_serve_moscow.text: Rival khans are tearing the Horde apart, and many princes and mirzas are leaving with their people to serve the Grand Prince of Moscow. There they are given lands, money and honour - so long as they serve with the sabre. You are invited to come along.
ev.mng_d_serve_moscow.go.ok: You cross the Oka with the mirza's troop. Ahead lie forests, churches and a strange tongue.
ev.mng_d_serve_moscow.stay.ok: You do not go. The steppe grows poorer, but it is your steppe.
ev.mng_d_mv_karakorum.title: To Karakorum
ev.mng_d_mv_karakorum.text: The new capital on the Orkhon needs everyone: herdsmen for the khan's herds, drivers for the caravans, men for the relay stations. They say silver flows like a river there, and in the bazaar you can buy anything under the Sky.
ev.mng_d_mv_karakorum.go.ok: You pitch your yurt by the walls of Karakorum. All around, the ring of hammers and the din of five languages.
ev.mng_d_mv_karakorum.stay.ok: You stay in your home pastures. It is quieter here.
ev.mng_d_mv_west.title: West with Batu
ev.mng_d_mv_west.text: The Ulus of Jochi is setting up its new seat on the Volga, and thousands of families are moving there with their yurts and herds - to "the land as far as the hooves of Mongol horses will reach". The road crosses half the world.
ev.mng_d_mv_west.go.ok: After a year on the road you see the Volga - wider than any river you have known.
ev.mng_d_mv_west.stay.ok: You see the wagons off as far as the pass and return to your hearth.
ev.mng_d_mv_khanbaliq.title: The court moves to China
ev.mng_d_mv_khanbaliq.text: Khubilai has moved the capital to Khanbaliq, and noyans, guardsmen, craftsmen and scribes are following him. The old Mongols grumble that the khan has turned Chinese. But there lie service, silver and silk.
ev.mng_d_mv_khanbaliq.go.ok: You ride in through gates as high as a cliff. Beyond them, straight streets run to the horizon.
ev.mng_d_mv_khanbaliq.stay.ok: You stay. The steppe is roomier without the khan.
ev.mng_d_mv_ilkhan.title: With Hülegü to Iran
ev.mng_d_mv_ilkhan.text: Hülegü is leading an army west - against the Ismaili fortresses and Baghdad - and families are going with the army. Ahead lie the warm pastures of Azerbaijan, where he means to sit as Ilkhan.
ev.mng_d_mv_ilkhan.go.ok: After two years on the road you pitch your yurt in a valley near Tabriz.
ev.mng_d_mv_ilkhan.stay.ok: You see the army off and stay with the herds.
ev.mng_d_mv_home.title: Longing for the Onon
ev.mng_d_mv_home.text: Foreign walls press in on you, the water here tastes wrong, and more and more often you dream of the Onon and the Kherlen. A caravan leaves for the east in a month.
ev.mng_d_mv_home.go.ok: You dismount on your native bank and kneel a long while in the grass.
ev.mng_d_mv_home.stay.ok: You stay. The longing does not pass, but you grow used even to that.
